description.narrative: Outcome 1: Local human rights actors are actively undertaking and facilitating initiatives on human rights and gender issues. Outcome 2: Disempowered people have increased access to justice through legal aid Outcome 3: Working Children increasigly enjoy fundamental human rights Outcome 4: State institutions are increasingly responsive to respecting human rights under their jurisdiction
Core support to the next phase of ASK's programme addressing the human rights situation in Bangladesh during 2017-2021.
Sidas stöd består av kärnstöd till nästkommande fas, 2017-2021, av Ain o Salish Kendra's initiativ med fokus på situationen i Bangladesh avseende mänskliga rättigheter.

During the course of the project, ASK continued to work as a human rights watchdog organisation documenting human rights violations at national as well as community levels. Simultaneously, the organisations has worked in the most marginalised communities providing legal support and carried out mobilisation-cum-awareness raising, building empowerment and resilience of the people.
The following are some of the major examples of results that have been achieved during the project's implementation (source: Project Completion Report).
- Human rights actors are mobilising the community people through initiatives to raise collective voices against human rights violations as well as are demanding actions for ensuring adequate and proper legal steps against the perpetrators. By the interventions of different groups, community people are claiming their rights from the state agencies.
- Women are actively participating and contributing in decision-making processes at the community and family level (e.g. local councils, village courts, school management committees, etc.).
- ASKs legal aid support services (legal advice, mediation, litigation, psycho-social counselling, support-shelter service) has increased access to justice for the disempowered people, especially women and children. The legal aid support and alternate dispute resolution (ADR/mediation) contributed greatly towards achievement of some of the results. In a significant number of these cases, the survivors received positive decisions by ADR (mediation) in favour of their claims, for which they regained trust towards the formal and informal justice system. Many were even able to receive their dower money (alimony) from their husbands while many were able to receive compensation following disputes; both the dower money and compensations proved to be beneficial to their survival and livelihood.
It is noteworthy that ASK served twice the target amount set during this reporting period, through ASKs intervention.
- Human rights violations, including violations of civil and political rights, were documented, disseminated, and immediately responded to generate public opinion and draw the attention of relevant authorities.
- ASK contributed to strengthening the National Human Rights Commission, Bangladesh (NHRC) by increasing its interaction with local human rights defenders and CSOs and developing assessment reports on its performance as per the national and international standards.
- ASK advocacy and networking at different levels have increased the governments involvement in the UN human rights mechanism. The government also addressed ASKs demand to adopt an action plan to implement commitments of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) by arranging multiple consultations with line ministries, selective CSOs, and development partners and outlining the implementation plan.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
